Blockhold · September 9, 2026

Light with a clearer identity.

Independent beams, distinct Seraph forms, softer signatures, and range you can trust. Then: give your level-25 roster new challenges and your heroes meaningful choices.

Seraph comparisonRange & placementWhat comes next
Implemented in this release

Seven forms. One direct beam per target.

Every beam starts at the Seraph’s heart. Upgrades increase the target count from 3 to 7; each target must be in tower range and visible. Damage, cost and firing rate stay the same. Void keeps its established shapes.

Staged captures from the actual game renderer, using identical positions. These illustrate forms and targeting, not difficulty or device performance.

Motion without the jolt

Wings ease between idle and firing. Rings rotate continuously. Upgrades settle gently. Dawnfall and Eclipse no longer shake the camera, pulse the whole tower, or stack the sharp signature cue. Dawnfall also loses its deliberate hit stop. A light column and violet halo fade in and out; separate soft chords replace the bass impact.

Short, silent captures of the real animations in a controlled scene. Combat is staged; audio changes are synthesized in the game.

A radius that follows the terrain.

Range follows each terrain cell and stops at voids and map edges. Already elevated plots show a disabled raise option explaining that the high-ground bonus is active.

The little gold lines are placement previews for tower combinations and Beacon bonuses. They now clear when selection changes or menus close, and the tooltip explains them.

Proposed next releases · not added to the game yet

After 25: new decisions before a longer grind.

The last roster unlock is at 25, and the account cap is currently 40. Simply extending the XP curve to 50 would mean another 26,800 XP—about 56 repeat Normal clears of a 30-wave map before bonuses. Fill that gap with distinct challenges.

01 · Next content release

Boss hunts + hero paths

Short, replayable hunts with visible phases and Casual / Normal / Veteran settings. Bring Ossuary and Veil Empress forward from deep endless waves.

02 · Mastery progression

Selected tier-six forms

Family challenges unlock Mythics at 50. Prototype 15–25k additional gold in a run, one Mythic per shared defense. Tune before treating that price as final.

03 · Roster expansion

New roles, new arenas

One purpose-built boss arena, then a tower or hero with an action the existing roster cannot express. Keep normal campaign balance on five tiers.

More hero upgrades that change how you play

Specializations around milestones 30 / 35 / 40, earned through varied hero challenges. Change paths freely between battles; keep battle levels and signature ranks as your investment during a run.

Aldric

Bulwark: protect nearby soldiers with a visible standard.
Vanguard: mark heavy enemies and evolve the slam into a directional armor break.

Liora

Hawkeye: priority marks and a focused piercing volley.
Gale Warden: a persistent wind corridor that helps control airborne threats.

Zephyra

Tempest: wider coverage through a storm field.
Riftbinder: reveal phased enemies and open a bounded focus-fire window.

Prism Warden

Three visible shield pylons. Split your fire to break them, then concentrate on the exposed core. No permanent damage-type immunity.

Ashen Conductor

A road pulse marked several seconds ahead. Reposition the hero and soldiers, then burst during recovery. No tower deletion or endless silence.

Both bosses are concepts. Test multiple successful strategies, readable warnings, boss crowd-control recovery, touch input and co-op before release. Inspiration: Ninja Kiwi’s official notes frame new bosses around tower selection and placement; this roadmap applies that principle to Blockhold.

Design source: Blockhold’s existing parchment, wood and gold theme from src/style.css. See reviews/endgame-direction.md for the full proposal and balancing criteria.
